truth.the_law_this_round_adds: A CORRECT DECISION HAS A PRICE, AND THE PRICE IS SET BY OBSERVABILITY. Trial-in-a-copy decides every action at 1.0 for 14 ms plus one execution and learns nothing; keeping the lesson cuts 160 executions to 52 and costs 7.5 accuracy points, all of them on the three actions the world cannot show. The condition is never named (0/10); operational understanding is decisiveness, and decisiveness without soundness is the failure mode of the loop.
what_is_false_in_the_claim: that one demonstration buys a decision: it scores 0.6125 and names nothing
that trial-and-learn is free: it is 29% cheaper than choosing properly and 7.5 points worse, concentrated exactly where the deciding fact is invisible
that a chooser can beat the wall: 37 vs 52 executions on the answerable seven, and zero coverage on the three the world will not answer
that a creature is a store of actions: the only measured value of creature-like behaviour is choosing the next question, 29% of executions, bounded by answerability
